question: A community health worker screens a 20-month-old child. She finds his MUAC is 11.2 cm, his weight-for-height z-score is −2.5 SD, and there is no bilateral pedal oedema. Which of the following correctly classifies this child according to WHO criteria?

answers.text: Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) only, because weight-for-height z-score is above −3 SD.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. WHO SAM criteria require ANY ONE of: WHZ < −3 SD, MUAC <11.5 cm (in children 6–59 months), or bilateral pedal oedema. This child's MUAC of 11.2 cm is below the 11.5 cm threshold — he meets SAM criteria on MUAC alone.

answers.text: Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), because MUAC <11.5 cm is sufficient to diagnose SAM regardless of other criteria.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. WHO SAM diagnosis requires ANY ONE criterion: WHZ < −3 SD, MUAC <11.5 cm (6–59 months), or bilateral pedal oedema. MUAC of 11.2 cm alone establishes SAM. This child needs immediate inpatient or CMAM referral.

answers.text: Normal nutritional status, because the child has no oedema and only borderline MUAC.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. MUAC <11.5 cm meets the WHO SAM threshold. The absence of oedema is relevant (oedema indicates kwashiorkor) but does not override the MUAC criterion.

answers.text: SAM can only be diagnosed if all three criteria — WHZ < −3 SD, MUAC <11.5 cm, and bilateral oedema — are simultaneously present.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. WHO diagnostic criteria require ANY ONE of the three indicators, not all three simultaneously. Meeting a single criterion is sufficient for SAM diagnosis.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key rule: SAM = ANY ONE of WHZ < −3 SD, MUAC <11.5 cm (6–59 mo), or bilateral pedal oedema. ANY ONE criterion is sufficient — not all three needed simultaneously.
Well done. MUAC <11.5 cm alone is sufficient for SAM diagnosis — a critical field-applicable criterion, especially when scales and height boards are unavailable.
